BLACK MARKET FUEL

By: Nicky Troll | Paid

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
There’s big money to made in the fuel industry – especially if you break the rules. Carte Blanche goes undercover to expose black market fuel operations.

Summary:
Fuel is like liquid gold on the black market. We’ve exposed many criminal syndicate MO’s over the years – from diesel skimming to hijacking petrol tankers and robbing petrol depots.

In recent years, the Transnet Pipelines were targeted – but with a clamp down on pipeline theft – the black market for fuel has evolved. We’re talking fuel spiking on an industrial level coupled with cross-border tax fraud – it’s lucrative industry when the players don’t hesitate to get their hands dirty.

But at what cost?

Further information:
THE MORAL OF THIS STORY IS THE FUEL INDUSTRY IS DIRTY - AND IT COSTS THE COUNTRY BILLIONS OF RANDS IN LOST TAX REVENUE.

There are three key elements here:
1. Transnet Pipeline – the evolution of fuel theft, the outrageous MOs and the crack down –There’s already a lot of footages and we can do a chopper flight with Waal to give this section an action element. As the door closes on these thieves, an entire new illicit industry taken over the black market.

2. Spiking is NO Myth – the market is still flooded with cheap fuel, but it isn’t from the thieves. The biggest suppliers of cheap diesel are able to undercut the market because they are not selling diesel – it’s a blend of diesel, paraffin and sometimes even water. In true CB investigative style – I’ve gone undercover and taken samples – we’ve done the testing and the results reveal that not only are these players mixing in paraffin – they are doing it in a way that is near impossible to trace.
** I’ve done two samples so far. The one company Bidvest has tested as well, and then there’s been another batch taken in a roadblock – we have three samples on the company. For the story I’d like to take three more samples from three different places to say we personally tested 5.
** My initial idea to order a truck and test on the spot is not going to work because I think the likelihood of the supplier sending a dodgy load on the first order is low and I feel it will take too much effort and I’m not guaranteed a result.

CALLS TO DODGY SUPPLIERS TO SHOW THE EXTENT OF QUESTIONABLY CHEAP DIESEL
I’ve recorded calls to a number of fuel suppliers – most offering below the regulated price, some even openly offering a “blended” product.

CASE STUDY – PIET VAN DYK – LEBOMBO BORDER
Piet has a filling station close to the Lebombo border post in Komatipoort – he also supplies farmers in the area. Last year October – his clients picked up problems with diesel - bakkies / farming equipment gave engine trouble (some clips available, mechanical / engineering reports done for all claims)

The diesel came from a supplier in Kempton Park. Piet van Dyk sent off samples for testing – the diesel was mixed with high quantities of paraffin. Van Dyk’s insurance covered his clients damage totally R15 million.

INVESTIGATIVE ELEMENT – We go in search of the dodgy supplier – we have the company details, their location and details of the drivers that worked for them.

THIS WILL LEAD US TO THE FACT THAT THEY ARE JUST ONE OF MANY DISTRIBUTORS THAT MIX.

HIDDEN ID ELEMENT – we interview a supplier that admits to mixing – but within the SANS regulations – he says if you don’t blend you can’t compete and his business won’t survive. Some wholesalers have closed up shop because they can’t beat black market offerings that are flooding the market.

DETAIL – Paraffin sales have increased dramatically – I have stats. But traders are greedy and looking for ways to beat the system. There is chemistry to it – some of the biggest spikers employ chemical engineers to remove the paraffin marker – making it impossible to pick up the mix with basic on the spot tests.

SCIENCE ELEMENT - lab tests – breaking down how they’re doing it and why it’s a problem. They will tell us of any 10 samples they get through their lab – probably 2 pass. The rest are all DODGE.

ACTION ELEMENT – Three sets of tests have been done on samples from specific fuel distributor. All Three tests have failed. In a multi-disciplinary take down – Bidvest, the HAWKS, SARS and of course CB – hit Elegant Fuels’ distribution / mixing plant.

BUT WHY SHOULD SOUTH AFRICANS CARE?!?!?

It’s about TAX FRAUD. When the blend with paraffin they make the diesel go further with a product that doesn’t have tax on it – making profits bigger.

BUT AGAIN these traders are greedy. And they are go far and wide to cut corners.

3. Overloading and Under-declaring – if you thought an action packed crackdown and confronts powered by undercover footage and scientific proof was sexy – wait for it - this is the sexiest element of the story – wholesalers are bringing fuel from Mozambique and under-declaring the quantities to save on tax and duties – this bunch of criminals steal from me and you! It’s tax money that is not paid. In an elaborate investigation where we get drone footage of the trucks by passing the weighbridges. Financially doesn’t make sense to load in Mozambique and distribute in Gauteng – you could get the same prices as getting fuel from DBN – without trucks being stuck at the borders or loading bays – the only way it makes any financial sense is if they’re not overloading and under-declaring.

UNDERCOVER ELEMENT – this scam is made possible by dodgy clearing agents and fake paperwork. We go undercover to meet with a clearing agent that will give us the low down – I’ve got one on-camera already but will aim to do a second one this week. Having an inside man is one part, the second is getting the paperwork. For this, you need someone on the Mozambique side to supply you with blank loading papers that the drivers jippo with the under declared quantities. We have a contact that explains all of this, we negotiated to buy a blank paper but the price went up. I have voice recordings, and copies of duplicate papers showing the fraud. I also have an insider interview to explain how it all works.

SUMMARY OF ELEMENTS
1. UNDERCOVER – BUYING FUEL (5)
2. INVESTIGATION - SCIENCE – LAB TESTS – THE SCALE OF IT
3. INSIDER INTERVIEW – A WHOLESALER THAT MIXES – ADMITS TO BREAKING THE RULES TO SURVIVE – PAINTS A PICTURE OF THE INDUSTRY – TENSION – YOU CAN’t BEAT THEM SO JOIN THEM
4. INVESTIGATION – TRACKING AND TRACING THE DODGY SUPPLIER LINKED TO CASE STUDY
5. UNDERCOVER – ATTEMPT TO BUY DODGY BORDER PAPERS - VOICE NOTES
6. INSIDER INTERIVEW – CROSS BORDER PAPER WORK
7. UNDERCOVER – MEETING CLEARING AGENT
8. ACTION – RAID A WHOLESALER THAT IS MIXING DIESEL
9. ACTION – PIPELINE SUCCESSES - DRONE FOOTAGE OF PIPELINE OPERATIONS // CHOPPER RIDE ALONG PIPELINE // ALSO TO SHOW DODGY DEPOTS
10. POSSIBLE ACTION – ROADBLOCK TO TEST AND CHECK OVERLOADING AT KOMATIPOORT


Extra Budget Items:

EXTRA BUDGET
o Research budget – already approved
(I haven’t used all of it – I’ve been to Komatipoort twice already for research, Witbank once, but I haven’t been charged for the tests yet – R26k approved, I’m sitting at about R10k used)
o Presenter Shoot days – I’ll need 4 days, plus a travel day.
o DAY 1. THE RAID ON THE MIXER.
o DAY 2 & 3. IN GAUTENG & CHOPPER WITH WAAL (security, transnet or a fuel traders association, science guys, mixing wholesaler hidden ID, tracking the company that linked to Piet van Dyk)
o DAY 4 & 5 – drive to Komatipoort – shoot Lebombo elements – Piet van Dyk, the border insider explaining paper work, general links and shots of the border. (komatipoort is 4.5 hourse one way)
o Accommodation in Komatipoort for crew for one night (R1600 x 4) + travel (R3290 for km) + tolls and S&T

STRUCTURE: BLACK MARKET FUEL…

VO: Liquid Gold…. easy to trade… difficult to trace… always in demand…

LINK: I'm talking about the fuel industry in an energy hungry country. It's a huge market which is open to ruthless operators that are willing to break the rules, cut corners and look the other way, all in the name of profit.

MIXER: If you don't have a conscience, you can make a lot of money easily.

VO: This month's long investigation plays out on multiple levels.

We’ve covered over 4000 kilometers, gone undercover, spent time in laboratories, and attended stake-outs. We’ve searched for the alleged culprits and even caught some red-handed.

UPSOUND MAC: SHOUTING SOMETHING AT MORRIS AS HE SPEEDS OFF…

VO: The Illicit fuel trade happens on three levels - from the straight up theft of millions of litres…

to stretching profit margins by mixing up blends of diesel.…..

and a cross-border tax fraud operation that’s never been captured on camera. Until now.

But, our investigation starts with black market fuel at its most basic level: theft. From diesel skimming to hijacking petrol tankers, and targeting fuel pipelines - we’ve exposed them all before.

PAUSE - VISUAL MOMENT

VO: Hitting underground pipelines - is by far the most labour intensive, but also, the most, lucrative.

WAAL: They will do one thing. We will stop the loophole. It will open up a new loophole. We will close that loophole

VO: Waal de Waal is a security specialist. His company is tasked with protecting Transnet’s fuel pipeline network.

UPSOUND JUMP JUMP - HANG ON JUMP JUMP

VO: He’s battling criminal syndicates hot tapping directly onto fuel pipelines, concealing flow bins in trucks, and going as far as digging underground tunnels to tap in.

UPSOUND from tunnel - then you can see the whole down there

VO: Intelligence driven operations have been adapted, utilising ground and air teams, to meet the ever changing criminal MO.

UPSOUND WAAL – listen carefully my friend, i’m coming for you

MUSIC MOMENT…

VO: Despite a crackdown on the syndicates feeding the black market with stolen fuel, questionably cheap diesel is still in circulation.

Our investigation leads us to a mid-level wholesaler, who agreed to share some trade secrets, as long as we hid his identity. These are his actual words, spoken by an actor.

MAC: Do you your business cutting corners to make money?
MIXER: Most definitely. There’s no way we can compete // the margins are just too low // we started blending diesel with paraffin

VO: This is the second level of illicit fuel - spiking… blending… mixing… adulterated diesel…is the chemistry of black market fuel.

Simply put, it’s when another product is mixed in with the diesel – usually an untaxed or duty free substance like paraffin. It means dodgy operators can improve profit margins by stretching their diesel- saving around R6 a litre in taxes .

Under quality regulations, diesel can include up to 5% paraffin. Anything over that, is not allowed.

MIXER: There's enough margin to be made. Even with a little bit of blending, you can stay afloat.

VO: But, some mixers whip up blends with paraffin ratios ranging from 35 to 65%.

MIXER: These guys are just out to kill it. // You get dirty diesel in the sense of dog crap, that is cutting the lifespan of that engine, in half. it's just greed for money.

RICHARD: // It's gotten very, very big in the last couple of years. We've seen an increase in // the amount of illicit mixing in the country.

VO: Richard Friend works for a global leader in fuel integrity services with a focus on security.

RICHARD: We look to make sure that people don't break the law. We provide all the forensic and scientific equipment and technology that goes into the adulterants in the the fuel industry.

VO: In South Africa , all paraffin must be spiked with a special security marker making it detectable in other substances like diesel.

Basic test kits can pick up this marker - but if the special security tracer isn’t there, the result will be negative - EVEN if it contains paraffin. The test looks for the marker, not paraffin.

Dodgy diesel suppliers know this and are finding ways to cheat the system.

AUDIO BREAK - PIET INTRO

VO: Mpumulanga Fuel Trader Piet van Dyk sells diesel to bulk customers from farmers to transporters. Last year, he received 80 000 litres from a regular supplier in Gauteng called Nicview Investments.

PIET: we did the normal testing for paraffin // we found that there was no trace of that. And so we distribute it to our clients

BEGIN UPSOUND CAR BATTLING TO START UNDER PIET END WORD “clients”….

VO: But, within hours, Van Dyk was confronted by irate customers.

CAR UPSOUND

PIET: We got phone calls from the farmers we delivered to say there’s something wrong with the fuel.

VO: Van Dyk recalled the fuel he distributed immediately - he also sent in a sample for testing. The result showed it wasn’t in spec - despite passing the initial field test.

It resulted in a 15 million rand insurance claim against his business.

LINK: So the company that supplied Piet van Dyk out in Komatipoort lists an address somewhere in JHB, in Bredell

MAC: here’s 299…. HELLO?

VO: But inside the premises - there was no sign of NicView Investments - we called the number on the invoice.

CALL - MAC - where are your offices so that we can come see you there?
CALLER: 299 6th Avenue.
MAC: We're here….we’re at 299 - which one is your office, sir?
CALLER: Okay let me speak to the guys who are there, because I’m that there at the moment.
MAC: Ah - ok - no problem.

VO: Apparently no one was available - but the landlord told us NicView Investments had never been tenants.

Nicview Investments took legal action against Van Dyk for outstanding payments . Denying the supplied diesel, didn’t conform to the required specs, they challenged him to provide conclusive proof that their loads were substandard.

VISUAL BREAK - CHANGE OF SCENE - MUSIC CHANGE…

VO: But it’s not an isolated case and points to a far bigger issue in the supply of bulk fuel. Mixed fuel is certainly being sold - whether the buyer knows it or not..

In this audio clip, a fuel supplier openly offers blended diesel to a potential customer, he’s speaking to for the very first time.

UPSOUND CALL:
SUPPLIER: Ek kan, ek kan vir jou blended kry.
ENGLISH: I can get blended for you.
CALLER: Die tracer, die marking is hy uit as jy hom geblend het? - REDO VOICE
ENGLISH: The tracer, the marking, is that out if it blended?
SUPPLIER: oh die tracer - hy’s uit, hy’s uit, hy’s uit.
ENGLISH: Oh, the tracer, it’s out, it’s out.

VO: When it comes to investigating illicit fuel, identifying diesel blends is becoming increasingly tricky.

RICHARD: They look to try and remove or negate the marker. Thankfully, our marker is multilayered, once you go through to the lab, you will pick up that the marker is there. // But what we are seeing now is that a lot of people are going towards unmarked paraffin

VO: Criminal enterprises peddling illicit fuel are flourishing. Their inventiveness is helping them dodge accountability and maximise profits. But the screws are tightening. In part two our investigation moves north, focussing on cross-border criminal operations and a showdown with one of the alleged ring leaders….

CLIFF HANGER…..END PART ONE


PART TWO

VO: We're investigating criminal networks raking in millions from dodgy diesel, from outright theft to illegal blending. But the latest trend is also the most brazen.

The third level of the illicit fuel trade is, fraud, on an international organised crime scale. It involves the most people and the most cash changing hands.

LINK: It's evolved to a level which has never been exposed until now. It's a simple scam that's all about overloading and under-declaring.

VO: A truck legally loads 60 000 litres of diesel in Mozambique, paid for at the proper pricing. The driver heads back to South Africa, but only declares 40 000 litres to SARS - CHEATING the country of around R120 000 in taxes.

And it’s not just one truck, here at Mpumalanga’s Lebombo border, it’s multiple trucks all the time.

VISUAL MOMENT OF TRUCK DRIVING PAST AND THEN MAC DRIVING PAST

VO: Our investigation here began months ago. Attempting to join all the dots, We scouted local depots, spotted suspect trucks and checked out local law enforcement.

MOMENT OF DRIVING… (MAYBE DRONE VAN KAR)

LINK: we’re going to meet a source…. and hope that he arrives.

SET UP SCENE - 3-5 sec…. source walks… while Mac asks.

MAC: how are you feeling?
SOURCE: mense word maar uitgehaal en dis maar ‘n gevaarlike bedryf, so ja stressvol…. ENGLISH: People are being taken out, it’s a dangerous industry. So yes, I’m feeling stressed.

VO: In just two years, the fuel industry here has grown dramatically.

SOURCE: Hierso is omtrent seker 100, 200, 300 tankers, wat tans hier laai, wat jy nooit gesien het nie, ek meen almal, die goedkoopste plek was maar Durban – dis omtrent soos ‘n tweede Durban nou hierdie kant.
ENGLISH: Here there’s about 100, 200, 300, tankers loading, that we never saw before. Everyone knew Durban was always the cheapest place. And now this is like a second Durban.

VO: The only financially viable way of distributing fuel from here to other parts of the country is to cheat on taxes and duties.

To prevent that, authorities monitor whether trucks are carrying their declared loads by weighing them.

LINK: one way of checking if a truck is overloaded is to bring it to the weighbridge. But the WEIGHBRIDGE has to be open and in working condition, and it seems it's hardly ever the case
SOURCE: As Die weegbrug nie werk nie, is dit tot hulle voordeel - want elke dag is daar mense, maar die trokke ry net verby.

VO: And our source says a lot of help is needed to pull it off.

SOURCE: Daar’s definitief clearing agents betrokke, maar nou kort hulle die ander partye om die res van die transaksie te voltooi./ eerstens is dit die SARS, die customs ouens, die polisie, die spietkops, mense by weegbrug, so hulle is almal definitief involved.
ENGLISH: There’s definitely clearing agents involved, but you need the other parties to complete the transaction. Firstly the SARS guys, the customs guys, the police, the traffic cops, the weighbridge people - everybody is definitely involved.

VO: Posing as dodgy transporters, we secured a meeting with a clearing agent working at the border.

He emphasised that the scam’s participants don’t come cheap.

UNDERCOVER AGENT (XML GEMAIL) CLIP 2
CLEARING AGENT: They can take 20, 30 000 - 10 000 - they usually not taking more than that //
they want cash - because it can’t go to the bank - it’s bribe money.

VO: But the scam also requires the right paperwork. In Mozambique, the truck driver is given a receipt and a report listing the correct amount of diesel loaded. It’s this document that needs to be altered to reduce the number of litres.

UNDERCOVER AGENT (XML GEMAIL) CLIP 1
CLEARING AGENT: // meanwhile you know on the truck
OPERATIVE: it’s more, ok
CLEARING AGENT: Those documents from Mozambique, they are the are most important documents.

VO: Important and for sale. In this clip, provided by our source, a Mozambican contact has got book of blank quantity sheets used to under-declare the diesel on the South African side of the border.

MOZ INSIDER: They preferred to sell the whole book. Each page they are asking for 750 rand. So I already got a book here with me. What they're just waiting, is just a payments.

SOURCE: Jou trok ry dan met die twee stelle papierwerk grens toe – aan die Mosambiekse kant stamp hulle, hulle 60 000 liter papierwerk. AAN die SA kant, betaal hy sy duties op die 40 000.
ENGLISH: Your truck drives to the border with the two sets of paperwork. On the Mozambique side, the 60 000 litre paperwork is stamped. On the SA side, he pays the duties on the 40 000.

VO: All bribes paid, the overloaded and under-declared truck makes off with at least R100 000 in clean profit stolen from the South African government.

It’s a crime trend now on law enforcement's radar. Security specialists contracted by Transnet have joined forces with a small group of handpicked SARS & HAWKS officers. Waal de Waal is running this project.

MAC: Why do you think the modus operandi is constantly evolving and changing?
WAAL: That's organized crime.// it will evolve all the time, you can minimize it.// you just need to be two ahead of them with the your expertize.

DAY TO NIGHT TRANSITION…
VO: Overloaded trucks often move under the cover of darkness.

STAKE OUT STING
LINK: //There's a sting operation that’s taking place // We're looking for Waal de Waal to get a bit more information as to what's going to be happening tonight, They don't stand in plain sight.
DRIVING & LOOKING….
LINK: Looks like they just stop the area. //
WAAL: Evening Mac!

WAAL: We've got two trucks coming from Matola, some of our suspects. So we foresee that they're not going to follow the procedure at the border post.
WAAL: We've got agents from the other side following the truck up to the South African side. And we've got a surveillance team //we've got our tactical team.

VO: They’re keeping a low profile, unsure of who to trust in a place where news travels fast.

WAAL: I don't want this police to because I don't trust those fuckers. **AUDIO BEEP FUCKERS **

VO: Six hours into the stake-out - the first suspect truck is spotted.

RADIO: Ok, Waal, are you behind him?
WAAL RADIO - / ek is net hier agter die cops - ek wil nie aandag trek nie - passop die lig.
ENGLISH: Yes, he’s a bit ahead of me, I’m just here behind the cops, I don’t want to draw attention. Be careful with that light.
CONFIRM - hy was JXD? OK you can take him.
ENGLISH: Confirm - it was JXT up in ahead?
ENGLISH It’s JXT.
WAAL: ENGLISH: Ok, then that’s our truck.

VO: The driver refuses to pull over, even trying to over take the police!

MAC: // either he’s scared, or khe knows exactly what’s going or he knows he’s been caught but he’s making it difficult for the police to stop him.
SHOT OF CHASE ON DIRT ROAD…

VO: The driver eventually stops just short of the depot. The truck is searched, while SARS does the calculations and the driver’s face, says it all.

And, in the background, an unknown man pays close attention.

WAAL: Who you?
MORRIS: It’s coming to park at our yard?
WAAL: I'm asking you who you. Who are you?
Morris: MORRIS
WAAL: Who? Okay, is this is your truck. Moros
Morris: No, no. We work together
WAAL: Morris Let's start over again. Morris Are you the boss? Morris
MORRIS: No, I'm the manager. //

VO: But he’s not just a manager, he’s the boss: Morris Musekwa also known as “Silent Killer” - the CEO of Locktrans, owner of the truck and the depot.

MAC: This is what we hear is your business model overloading and under declaring, sir, you're giving up your right of reply. You've been caught. // Would you rather run away from us? Oh, well, I guess the Weighbridge will tell us the truth what’s happening.

VO: As we head to the weighbridge – it was clear word was getting out, a BMW pulled from another one of De Waal’s suspect depots and followed us.

DRIVING MOMENT TO GET US TO WEIGHBRIGDE?

MAC: Today the Weighbridge was working and after we stop these trucks on our way here, there was a white BMW that sped past us and we were wondering where it was going. They got here before us and lo and behold, when we get to suddenly the weighbridge is not working. You do the math.

WAAL: But it's not working. I just want to know when did it broke down and when did you report?

VO: Then, a second truck belonging to Morris arrives at the weighbridge.

LINK: We don't need to weigh this truck because here's the paperwork. 40,000 declared South Africa. This is how much you loaded in Mozambique. 62,000 people were going to die. You didn't get a chance to get rid of them And now we've caught them red handed.

VO: Silent Killer Morris is still lingering, so we approach him a second time.

MAC: Now you've been caught red handed. The paperwork doesn't like under the clearing. 40,000, 60,000. Big difference.

VO: Investigators later confirm that both trucks were overloaded: They initially declared 40 000 litres each - but were carrying a lot more .

WAAL: //we always knew that there was a bit of overloading in there and and a bit of mixing here and there. But to this scale, never I mean, this is an eye opener for for the country, for law enforcement, for everybody involved

VO: And as long as it continues, the country will continue losing millions in tax. Money stolen by criminal enterprises facilitated by those meant to enforce the law.

Carte Blanche goes undercover to expose black market fuel operations. Summary: Fuel is like liquid gold on the black market. We’ve exposed many criminal syndicate MO’s over the years – from diesel skimming to hijacking petrol tankers and robbing petrol depots. In recent years, the Transnet Pipelines were targeted – but with a clamp down on pipeline theft – the black market for fuel has evolved. We’re talking fuel spiking on an industrial level coupled with cross-border tax fraud – it’s lucrative industry when the players don’t hesitate to get their hands dirty. But at what cost? Further information: THE MORAL OF THIS STORY IS THE FUEL INDUSTRY IS DIRTY - AND IT COSTS THE COUNTRY BILLIONS OF RANDS IN LOST TAX REVENUE. There are three key elements here: 1. Transnet Pipeline – the evolution of fuel theft, the outrageous MOs and the crack down –There’s already a lot of footages and we can do a chopper flight with Waal to give this section an action element. As the door closes on these thieves, an entire new illicit industry taken over the black market. 2. Spiking is NO Myth – the market is still flooded with cheap fuel, but it isn’t from the thieves. The biggest suppliers of cheap diesel are able to undercut the market because they are not selling diesel – it’s a blend of diesel, paraffin and sometimes even water. In true CB investigative style – I’ve gone undercover and taken samples – we’ve done the testing and the results reveal that not only are these players mixing in paraffin – they are doing it in a way that is near impossible to trace. ** I’ve done two samples so far. The one company Bidvest has tested as well, and then there’s been another batch taken in a roadblock – we have three samples on the company. For the story I’d like to take three more samples from three different places to say we personally tested 5. ** My initial idea to order a truck and test on the spot is not going to work because I think the likelihood of the supplier sending a dodgy load on the first order is low and I feel it will take too much effort and I’m not guaranteed a result. CALLS TO DODGY SUPPLIERS TO SHOW THE EXTENT OF QUESTIONABLY CHEAP DIESEL I’ve recorded calls to a number of fuel suppliers – most offering below the regulated price, some even openly offering a “blended” product. CASE STUDY – PIET VAN DYK – LEBOMBO BORDER Piet has a filling station close to the Lebombo border post in Komatipoort – he also supplies farmers in the area. Last year October – his clients picked up problems with diesel - bakkies / farming equipment gave engine trouble (some clips available, mechanical / engineering reports done for all claims) The diesel came from a supplier in Kempton Park. Piet van Dyk sent off samples for testing – the diesel was mixed with high quantities of paraffin. Van Dyk’s insurance covered his clients damage totally R15 million. INVESTIGATIVE ELEMENT – We go in search of the dodgy supplier – we have the company details, their location and details of the drivers that worked for them. THIS WILL LEAD US TO THE FACT THAT THEY ARE JUST ONE OF MANY DISTRIBUTORS THAT MIX. HIDDEN ID ELEMENT – we interview a supplier that admits to mixing – but within the SANS regulations – he says if you don’t blend you can’t compete and his business won’t survive. Some wholesalers have closed up shop because they can’t beat black market offerings that are flooding the market. DETAIL – Paraffin sales have increased dramatically – I have stats. But traders are greedy and looking for ways to beat the system. There is chemistry to it – some of the biggest spikers employ chemical engineers to remove the paraffin marker – making it impossible to pick up the mix with basic on the spot tests. SCIENCE ELEMENT - lab tests – breaking down how they’re doing it and why it’s a problem. They will tell us of any 10 samples they get through their lab – probably 2 pass. The rest are all DODGE. ACTION ELEMENT – Three sets of tests have been done on samples from specific fuel distributor. All Three tests have failed. In a multi-disciplinary take down – Bidvest, the HAWKS, SARS and of course CB – hit Elegant Fuels’ distribution / mixing plant. BUT WHY SHOULD SOUTH AFRICANS CARE?!?!? It’s about TAX FRAUD. When the blend with paraffin they make the diesel go further with a product that doesn’t have tax on it – making profits bigger. BUT AGAIN these traders are greedy. And they are go far and wide to cut corners. 3. Overloading and Under-declaring – if you thought an action packed crackdown and confronts powered by undercover footage and scientific proof was sexy – wait for it - this is the sexiest element of the story – wholesalers are bringing fuel from Mozambique and under-declaring the quantities to save on tax and duties – this bunch of criminals steal from me and you! It’s tax money that is not paid. In an elaborate investigation where we get drone footage of the trucks by passing the weighbridges. Financially doesn’t make sense to load in Mozambique and distribute in Gauteng – you could get the same prices as getting fuel from DBN – without trucks being stuck at the borders or loading bays – the only way it makes any financial sense is if they’re not overloading and under-declaring. UNDERCOVER ELEMENT – this scam is made possible by dodgy clearing agents and fake paperwork. We go undercover to meet with a clearing agent that will give us the low down – I’ve got one on-camera already but will aim to do a second one this week. Having an inside man is one part, the second is getting the paperwork. For this, you need someone on the Mozambique side to supply you with blank loading papers that the drivers jippo with the under declared quantities. We have a contact that explains all of this, we negotiated to buy a blank paper but the price went up. I have voice recordings, and copies of duplicate papers showing the fraud. I also have an insider interview to explain how it all works. SUMMARY OF ELEMENTS 1. UNDERCOVER – BUYING FUEL (5) 2. INVESTIGATION - SCIENCE – LAB TESTS – THE SCALE OF IT 3. It's a huge market which is open to ruthless operators that are willing to break the rules, cut corners and look the other way, all in the name of profit. MIXER: If you don't have a conscience, you can make a lot of money easily. VO: This month's long investigation plays out on multiple levels. UPSOUND MAC: SHOUTING SOMETHING AT MORRIS AS HE SPEEDS OFF… VO: The Illicit fuel trade happens on three levels - from the straight up theft of millions of litres… to stretching profit margins by mixing up blends of diesel.….. and a cross-border tax fraud operation that’s never been captured on camera. Until now. But, our investigation starts with black market fuel at its most basic level: theft. From diesel skimming to hijacking petrol tankers, and targeting fuel pipelines - we’ve exposed them all before. PAUSE - VISUAL MOMENT VO: Hitting underground pipelines - is by far the most labour intensive, but also, the most, lucrative. WAAL: They will do one thing. We will stop the loophole. It will open up a new loophole. We will close that loophole VO: Waal de Waal is a security specialist. His company is tasked with protecting Transnet’s fuel pipeline network. UPSOUND JUMP JUMP - HANG ON JUMP JUMP VO: He’s battling criminal syndicates hot tapping directly onto fuel pipelines, concealing flow bins in trucks, and going as far as digging underground tunnels to tap in. UPSOUND from tunnel - then you can see the whole down there VO: Intelligence driven operations have been adapted, utilising ground and air teams, to meet the ever changing criminal MO. UPSOUND WAAL – listen carefully my friend, i’m coming for you MUSIC MOMENT… VO: Despite a crackdown on the syndicates feeding the black market with stolen fuel, questionably cheap diesel is still in circulation. Our investigation leads us to a mid-level wholesaler, who agreed to share some trade secrets, as long as we hid his identity. These are his actual words, spoken by an actor. MAC: Do you your business cutting corners to make money? MIXER: Most definitely. There’s no way we can compete // the margins are just too low // we started blending diesel with paraffin VO: This is the second level of illicit fuel - spiking… blending… mixing… adulterated diesel…is the chemistry of black market fuel. Simply put, it’s when another product is mixed in with the diesel – usually an untaxed or duty free substance like paraffin. It means dodgy operators can improve profit margins by stretching their diesel- saving around R6 a litre in taxes . Under quality regulations, diesel can include up to 5% paraffin. Anything over that, is not allowed. MIXER: There's enough margin to be made. Even with a little bit of blending, you can stay afloat. VO: But, some mixers whip up blends with paraffin ratios ranging from 35 to 65%. MIXER: These guys are just out to kill it. // You get dirty diesel in the sense of dog crap, that is cutting the lifespan of that engine, in half. it's just greed for money. RICHARD: // It's gotten very, very big in the last couple of years. We've seen an increase in // the amount of illicit mixing in the country. VO: Richard Friend works for a global leader in fuel integrity services with a focus on security. RICHARD: We look to make sure that people don't break the law. We provide all the forensic and scientific equipment and technology that goes into the adulterants in the the fuel industry. VO: In South Africa , all paraffin must be spiked with a special security marker making it detectable in other substances like diesel. Basic test kits can pick up this marker - but if the special security tracer isn’t there, the result will be negative - EVEN if it contains paraffin. The test looks for the marker, not paraffin. Dodgy diesel suppliers know this and are finding ways to cheat the system. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): There’s big money to made in the fuel industry – especially if you break the rules. Carte Blanche goes undercover to expose black market fuel operations.
metadata.Summary: Fuel is like liquid gold on the black market. We’ve exposed many criminal syndicate MO’s over the years – from diesel skimming to hijacking petrol tankers and robbing petrol depots. In recent years, the Transnet Pipelines were targeted – but with a clamp down on pipeline theft – the black market for fuel has evolved. We’re talking fuel spiking on an industrial level coupled with cross-border tax fraud – it’s lucrative industry when the players don’t hesitate to get their hands dirty. But at what cost?
metadata.Further information: THE MORAL OF THIS STORY IS THE FUEL INDUSTRY IS DIRTY - AND IT COSTS THE COUNTRY BILLIONS OF RANDS IN LOST TAX REVENUE. There are three key elements here: 1. Transnet Pipeline – the evolution of fuel theft, the outrageous MOs and the crack down –There’s already a lot of footages and we can do a chopper flight with Waal to give this section an action element. As the door closes on these thieves, an entire new illicit industry taken over the black market. 2. Spiking is NO Myth – the market is still flooded with cheap fuel, but it isn’t from the thieves. The biggest suppliers of cheap diesel are able to undercut the market because they are not selling diesel – it’s a blend of diesel, paraffin and sometimes even water. In true CB investigative style – I’ve gone undercover and taken samples – we’ve done the testing and the results reveal that not only are these players mixing in paraffin – they are doing it in a way that is near impossible to trace. ** I’ve done two samples so far. The one company Bidvest has tested as well, and then there’s been another batch taken in a roadblock – we have three samples on the company. For the story I’d like to take three more samples from three different places to say we personally tested 5. ** My initial idea to order a truck and test on the spot is not going to work because I think the likelihood of the supplier sending a dodgy load on the first order is low and I feel it will take too much effort and I’m not guaranteed a result. CALLS TO DODGY SUPPLIERS TO SHOW THE EXTENT OF QUESTIONABLY CHEAP DIESEL I’ve recorded calls to a number of fuel suppliers – most offering below the regulated price, some even openly offering a “blended” product. CASE STUDY – PIET VAN DYK – LEBOMBO BORDER Piet has a filling station close to the Lebombo border post in Komatipoort – he also supplies farmers in the area. Last year October – his clients picked up problems with diesel - bakkies / farming equipment gave engine trouble (some clips available, mechanical / engineering reports done for all claims) The diesel came from a supplier in Kempton Park. Piet van Dyk sent off samples for testing – the diesel was mixed with high quantities of paraffin. Van Dyk’s insurance covered his clients damage totally R15 million. INVESTIGATIVE ELEMENT – We go in search of the dodgy supplier – we have the company details, their location and details of the drivers that worked for them. THIS WILL LEAD US TO THE FACT THAT THEY ARE JUST ONE OF MANY DISTRIBUTORS THAT MIX. HIDDEN ID ELEMENT – we interview a supplier that admits to mixing – but within the SANS regulations – he says if you don’t blend you can’t compete and his business won’t survive. Some wholesalers have closed up shop because they can’t beat black market offerings that are flooding the market. DETAIL – Paraffin sales have increased dramatically – I have stats. But traders are greedy and looking for ways to beat the system. There is chemistry to it – some of the biggest spikers employ chemical engineers to remove the paraffin marker – making it impossible to pick up the mix with basic on the spot tests. SCIENCE ELEMENT - lab tests – breaking down how they’re doing it and why it’s a problem. They will tell us of any 10 samples they get through their lab – probably 2 pass. The rest are all DODGE. ACTION ELEMENT – Three sets of tests have been done on samples from specific fuel distributor. All Three tests have failed. In a multi-disciplinary take down – Bidvest, the HAWKS, SARS and of course CB – hit Elegant Fuels’ distribution / mixing plant. BUT WHY SHOULD SOUTH AFRICANS CARE?!?!? It’s about TAX FRAUD. When the blend with paraffin they make the diesel go further with a product that doesn’t have tax on it – making profits bigger. BUT AGAIN these traders are greedy. And they are go far and wide to cut corners. 3. Overloading and Under-declaring – if you thought an action packed crackdown and confronts powered by undercover footage and scientific proof was sexy – wait for it - this is the sexiest element of the story – wholesalers are bringing fuel from Mozambique and under-declaring the quantities to save on tax and duties – this bunch of criminals steal from me and you! It’s tax money that is not paid. In an elaborate investigation where we get drone footage of the trucks by passing the weighbridges. Financially doesn’t make sense to load in Mozambique and distribute in Gauteng – you could get the same prices as getting fuel from DBN – without trucks being stuck at the borders or loading bays – the only way it makes any financial sense is if they’re not overloading and under-declaring. UNDERCOVER ELEMENT – this scam is made possible by dodgy clearing agents and fake paperwork. We go undercover to meet with a clearing agent that will give us the low down – I’ve got one on-camera already but will aim to do a second one this week. Having an inside man is one part, the second is getting the paperwork. For this, you need someone on the Mozambique side to supply you with blank loading papers that the drivers jippo with the under declared quantities. We have a contact that explains all of this, we negotiated to buy a blank paper but the price went up. I have voice recordings, and copies of duplicate papers showing the fraud. I also have an insider interview to explain how it all works. SUMMARY OF ELEMENTS 1. UNDERCOVER – BUYING FUEL (5) 2. INVESTIGATION - SCIENCE – LAB TESTS – THE SCALE OF IT 3. INSIDER INTERVIEW – A WHOLESALER THAT MIXES – ADMITS TO BREAKING THE RULES TO SURVIVE – PAINTS A PICTURE OF THE INDUSTRY – TENSION – YOU CAN’t BEAT THEM SO JOIN THEM 4. INVESTIGATION – TRACKING AND TRACING THE DODGY SUPPLIER LINKED TO CASE STUDY 5. UNDERCOVER – ATTEMPT TO BUY DODGY BORDER PAPERS - VOICE NOTES 6. INSIDER INTERIVEW – CROSS BORDER PAPER WORK 7. UNDERCOVER – MEETING CLEARING AGENT 8. ACTION – RAID A WHOLESALER THAT IS MIXING DIESEL 9. ACTION – PIPELINE SUCCESSES - DRONE FOOTAGE OF PIPELINE OPERATIONS // CHOPPER RIDE ALONG PIPELINE // ALSO TO SHOW DODGY DEPOTS 10. POSSIBLE ACTION – ROADBLOCK TO TEST AND CHECK OVERLOADING AT KOMATIPOORT
